name: AXS-14 (Esreboxetine)
summary:
AXS-14 (esreboxetine) is the SS-enantiomer of reboxetine, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor Axsome licensed from Pfizer in January 2020 with US-only rights, for the management of fibromyalgia. The NDA submitted in May 2025 on Pfizer's two positive trials drew a Refuse to File in June 2025: the FDA accepted the fixed-dose Phase 3 with a 12-week primary endpoint but not the 8-week flexible-dose Phase 2 (Q1 2026 10-Q 0001193125-26-204274; FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-064267). Axsome started FORWARD (NCT07398417, 620 patients, randomized withdrawal after 12 weeks open-label on 8 mg, primary completion 2028-03 estimated) in January 2026 to address this, alongside an open-label safety study (NCT07637162, 2028-05), and plans to resubmit.
Price anchor: Savella (milnacipran), the only branded reuptake inhibitor labelled for fibromyalgia alone, at $3,572 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024 (before its first generic, launched March 2026), halved by the Part D rule. Uptake anchor: Savella's 2024 Medicare new starts, 4.20% a year of the treated-basis fibromyalgia pool, on a fibromyalgia-specific (ICD-10 M79.7) incidence of 0.12% of adults a year (second reader; the ICD-9 729.1 myalgia incidence was replaced).
Pfizer is owed tiered mid-single to low double-digit royalties and up to $323mm of milestones; the royalty is read at 4%, the bottom of 'mid-single', for netting once Axsome's cost block exists.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07398417 (book trials table): primary outcome 'Time from randomization to loss of therapeutic response'; Axsome Q2 2026 results deck (8-K 0001193125-26-341206, exhibit 2): 12-week open-label period on AXS-14 8 mg once daily, then responders randomized 1:1 to continue or switch to placebo for up to 12 weeks
therapy_mode.note: Daily oral maintenance for a chronic pain syndrome, and the trial measures loss of response on withdrawal, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07398417 primary outcome 'Time from randomization to loss of therapeutic response', design 'Randomized, Double, Treatment', start 2026-01-14. Axsome Q2 2026 deck (8-K 0001193125-26-341206, exhibit 2, book filing text): 'Open-label Period (12 weeks)', 'Double-blind Phase (up to 12 weeks)', 1:1 randomization of patients achieving response, AXS-14 8 mg. A maintenance, loss-of-response design for a daily oral drug in a chronic pain syndrome is chronic by the brief's definition.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Savella: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $59,322,983.07 over 16,606 beneficiaries = $3,572 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator: the house convention. Savella is the closest marketed comparator in the same disease and setting: a branded reuptake inhibitor (milnacipran, the most norepinephrine-leaning SNRI) labelled for fibromyalgia alone and sold against generic duloxetine and pregabalin, which is where AXS-14, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, will sit. It is the only fibromyalgia product in the book's CMS table. The spend covers 4.96 claims per beneficiary ($721 a claim), not a year, which matches the engine's stock recursion counting each start as a full year. The case for higher, and it is large: Axsome's own CNS brands read $4,686 (Auvelity) and $5,247 (Sunosi) per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand), 31% and 47% higher. Tonmya, the first new fibromyalgia drug in 16 years (launched 17 November 2025), lists at a WAC of $1,860 a month for the 60-count adult supply, $22,320 a year (Tonix, via pharmaphorum.com/news/tonix-launches-its-new-fibromyalgia-drug-us and panabee.com), and netted about $874 a prescription in Q2 2026 ($11.0mm over 12,592 prescriptions, Tonix Q2 2026 release, globenewswire.com 2026-08-10), about 2.4x Savella's halved $360 a claim. A new brand launched around 2029 is more likely to price near Tonmya or Auvelity than a 2009 brand. The case for lower: generic duloxetine and pregabalin cost a fraction of this, and payers may step AXS-14 behind them
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Savella, Part D 2024: $59,322,983.07 / 16,606 beneficiaries = $3,572.38, so 0.003572 mm USD; 82,321 claims = 4.96 per beneficiary, $720.63 a claim. Generic status: Savella was branded-only in 2024. Breckenridge launched generic milnacipran HCl tablets on 19 March 2026 and Glenmark an authorized generic the same day (Breckenridge release, prnewswire.com/news-releases/...-302718947.html; BW Healthcare World), described as the first US generic of Savella, with Savella at about $102.9mm of sales in the 12 months to January 2026; a Drugs.com summary suggesting generics from November 2017 could not be confirmed and conflicts with those releases. The book holds Savella's Orange Book use patent 7994220 to 2029-09-19 and no Paragraph IV record. CMS reports a brand's own claims under its brand name in any case, so the 2024 figure is a brand price, not generic-eroded; the generics are a case for lower pricing power by a 2030 launch, not a flaw in the figure. Auvelity ($77,071,789.99 / 16,448 = $4,686) and Sunosi ($21,025,660.84 / 4,007 = $5,247) are confirmed in the book (+31% and +47%), but they treat MDD and excessive sleepiness, not fibromyalgia. The brief anchors on the closest marketed comparator in the same disease and setting, so neither would be better sourced under the brief; they stay as case-for-higher evidence. Tonmya Q2 2026: $11mm net sales on 12,592 prescriptions confirmed (Tonix Q2 2026 release, globenewswire 2026-08-10), $874 a prescription; its $1,860 monthly WAC was not confirmed by my search, so no switch to a WAC anchor is made. Judgement labelled, case against given; confirmed.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices); Savella is Part D (lookup.py demand Savella, part D)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 comes off list, so net is $1,786 per patient-year. Cross-check: Tonmya's Q2 2026 net of about $874 a prescription against its $1,860 WAC is 53% off list, close to the convention for a new fibromyalgia brand (derived from Tonix's reported net sales and prescriptions; some prescriptions are the $930 30-count, so the true discount is somewhat smaller)
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is CMS Part D (lookup.py demand Savella, part 'D'), so the house value is 0.5 off list; direction right: net $1,786 per patient-year = 0.003572 x (1 - 0.5). The Tonmya cross-check: $11.0mm / 12,592 = $873.6 a prescription is confirmed; the 53% off its $1,860 WAC rests on a WAC I could not confirm, and the brief's convention does not depend on it.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Liu Y, Qian C, Yang M, 'Treatment Patterns Associated with ACR-Recommended Medications in the Management of Fibromyalgia in the United States', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2016;22(3):263-271, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.3.263, PMID 27003556 (MarketScan, 240,144 adults newly diagnosed 2009-2011): 'With the exception of duloxetine, discontinuation rates at 6 months were > 50% for all agents', milnacipran included, discontinuation being a supply gap of 90 days or more
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement: constant hazard from the six-month figure, 1 - (1 - 0.5)^(12/6) = 0.75 a year. The '>50%' makes it a floor for milnacipran and pregabalin. Consistent with Savella's CMS series: 4.96 claims per Part D beneficiary a year (lookup.py demand Savella, 2024), about five months on drug, and with Axsome's own statement that over 50% of fibromyalgia patients discontinue within the first year (FY2025 10-K). The same rate is used to back Savella's new starts out of its CMS series in penetration_peak_pct, so the two stay consistent. Case for lower: duloxetine kept more than half its patients at six months, and FORWARD's randomized withdrawal design selects responders, which a label built on it may favour. Case for higher: esreboxetine's own adverse events (insomnia 15.7%, constipation 17.2%, dry mouth 15.7% on drug in the 8-week Phase 2; Arnold LM et al., Clin Ther 2010;32(9):1618-1632, doi:10.1016/j.clinthera.2010.08.003)
discontinuation_pct.check: Liu 2016 (PMID 27003556, doi 10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.3.263) abstract via PubMed: 240,144 newly diagnosed adults (ICD-9 729.1, MarketScan 2009-2011); discontinuation = first supply gap of 90 days or more; 'With the exception of duloxetine, discontinuation rates at 6 months were > 50% for all agents', milnacipran included. 1 - (1 - 0.5)^2 = 0.75 a year, a floor. Axsome FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267), verbatim: 'over 50% of fibromyalgia patients discontinuing their treatment within the first year'. Savella 2024 claims per beneficiary 82,321 / 16,606 = 4.96. Arnold 2010 (PMID 20974319) adverse events confirmed: constipation 17.2%, insomnia 15.7%, dry mouth 15.7% on esreboxetine. Judgement labelled with both cases; confirmed.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07398417 (FORWARD) primary completion 2028-03 and NCT07637162 (open-label safety) 2028-05, both estimated (context file; book trials table). Axsome FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267) and Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-342360): Refuse to File received June 2025; FORWARD initiated 15 January 2026 to address the FDA's feedback; the NDA 'we plan to resubmit'
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. Axsome gives no topline or resubmission date in its filings or releases (book filing texts and a September 2026 search checked). Topline around mid-2028, a resubmission in the second half of 2028 once the open-label safety study completes, and a standard 12-month review for a new molecular entity (reboxetine was never approved in the US) put approval in the second half of 2029, so 2030 is the first full year. Case for 2029: a fast resubmission after a March 2028 completion and an early action date. Case for 2031: any enrolment slip in a 620-patient withdrawal study, or a second FDA objection after an RTF history. LOE: no molecule patent date is filed. Axsome's FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267, patents section) lists only pending US and foreign applications for AXS-14, so the engine's default applies: 12 years from this launch year, 2042. No date is written here because none is filed
forecast_start_year.check: defect review 2026-09-25: value unchanged; the note now states that no molecule patent date is filed and the engine's 12-year default applies; was 2030 (confirmed)

exus_multiple.source: Axsome FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267) and Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-342360), Pfizer licence: 'exclusive rights to develop and commercialize esreboxetine ... in the United States for the treatment of fibromyalgia'; 'an exclusive U.S. license'
exus_multiple.note: Axsome holds US rights only and no ex-US royalty from Pfizer is disclosed, so Axsome books nothing outside the US. Stated as 0.0 rather than null so the reason is on the row
exus_multiple.check: FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267), verbatim: 'an exclusive U.S. license to Pfizer's clinical and non-clinical data, and intellectual property for reboxetine'; 'exclusive rights to develop and commercialize esreboxetine ... in the U.S. for the treatment of fibromyalgia'; 'the exclusive right and sole responsibility of developing AXS-14 (esreboxetine) in the U.S. for the treatment of fibromyalgia and for other indications'; diligence obligations run 'in the United States'. No ex-US right or ex-US royalty to Axsome is disclosed. US rights only, so 0.0 (the engine then scales the pool by 1.0).

economics_share.source: Axsome Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-342360), note 'Exclusive License Agreement with Pfizer', and FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-064267): Pfizer received 82,019 shares and $3.0mm upfront (January 2020) and 'can also receive up to $323 million in regulatory and sales milestones, and tiered mid-single to low double-digit royalties on future sales related to the licensed products'; no milestones or royalties paid to date. Netted as the book nets a royalty the company pays: (margin - royalty) / margin, with the royalty at the bottom of the filed range, 4%, the book's reading of 'mid-single digit' (seltorexant and litifilimab seeds). Margin from Axsome's cost block, borrowed from Neurocrine (cogs 0.0182, sga 0.4042, rd 0.3551, other_costs 0): 1 - 0.7775 = 0.2225. (0.2225 - 0.04) / 0.2225 = 0.820225
economics_share.note: JUDGEMENT twice. (1) Tier: the range read at its bottom. The tiers rise to low double digits with sales; at 10% the share is 0.5506. (2) Margin: a comparator's, since Axsome's own FY2025 lines give a negative one (revenue $638.5mm, SG&A 89% of it, m = -0.2551; 10-K 0001193125-26-064267). Recompute when Axsome's filed margin turns positive. The up to $323mm of regulatory and sales milestones are not netted, as in the book's other royalty seeds
economics_share.check: struck at assembly on the Neurocrine cost block the reader's note named as illustrative: (0.2225 - 0.04) / 0.2225; the reader's value was None (confirmed)

prevalence.source: Walitt B et al., 'Three-Quarters of Persons in the US Population Reporting a Clinical Diagnosis of Fibromyalgia Do Not Satisfy Fibromyalgia Criteria: The 2012 National Health Interview Survey', PLoS One 2016;11(6):e0157235, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0157235, PMID 27281286: 1.78% of US adults report a clinical diagnosis of fibromyalgia. Applied to 266,978,268 US residents aged 18 and over (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP at 1 July 2024, the base epidemiology.csv uses for obesity): 4,752,213
prevalence.note: Not carried by the book (lookup.py pool Fibromyalgia and epidemiology.csv return nothing), so sourced here. Judgement: the clinically diagnosed population is the one a prescription reaches, and Savella's users, who set the peak, are drawn from it. A 2012 rate on a 2024 base. The criteria-based count from the same survey is almost the same size, 1.75% or 3.94mm of 225.7mm adults in 2012 (Walitt B et al., PLoS One 2015;10(9):e0138024, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0138024, PMID 26379048), but the two groups barely overlap: 73.5% of the diagnosed do not meet criteria and 73% of those meeting criteria have no fibromyalgia diagnosis. Axsome's 'approximately 17 million' (10-K; its deck cites Vincent et al. 2013) is a survey-based count not tied to a diagnosis, and is not used
prevalence.check: Walitt 2016 (PMID 27281286) abstract via PubMed: 'Of the 1.78% of persons reporting a clinical diagnosis, 73.5% did not meet NHIS fibromyalgia criteria', weighted to 225,726,257 adults. 0.0178 x 266,978,268 = 4,752,213. Walitt 2015 (PMID 26379048): 1.75%, 3.94mm of 225.7mm, 73% of criteria cases without a fibromyalgia diagnosis, confirmed. The 266,978,268 base is the one epidemiology.csv uses for obesity (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP). lookup.py pool Fibromyalgia returns nothing from the assumptions or epidemiology.csv, so the book does not carry it. The pool matches the label FORWARD implies: adults 18 or over with a fibromyalgia diagnosis (Q2 2026 deck). New case for lower, found in this check: Kaur 2026 (PMID 42238973, MarketScan, ICD-10 M79.7) puts the 2020 annual diagnosed adult prevalence at 0.44% in Commercial + Medicare and 0.90% in Medicaid, on at least two codes within the year, which misses patients not seen twice that year. Judgement labelled; confirmed.

incidence.source: Kaur M, Rudnik J, Meisner P, Williams A, Lauwerys B, 'Prevalence and incidence of fibromyalgia and associated severity in the United States using MarketScan', Pain Rep 2026;11(4):e1451, doi:10.1097/PR9.0000000000001451, PMID 42238973, PMC13229459 (full text read): annual incidence of diagnosed fibromyalgia in adults 18 and over was 0.12% (95% CI 0.12-0.12) in 2020 in MarketScan Commercial + Medicare, defined on ICD-10-CM M79.7 (the fibromyalgia-specific code) as a first recorded code with none in the preceding 12 months, confirmed by a second code within a year, among adults continuously enrolled for 12 months. 0.12% x 266,978,268 US adults (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP at 1 July 2024) = 320,374
incidence.note: Judgement: the Commercial + Medicare adult rate applied to all US adults, and the latest year the paper reports. Replaces Weir 2006 (PMID 16755239), whose cases were first claims coded ICD-9-CM 729.1, 'myalgia and myositis, unspecified', a broad myalgia code; its 2,424,163 a year was 51% of the diagnosed prevalence, a two-year diagnosed duration for a chronic disease. This rate implies about 14.8 years (4,752,213 / 320,374). Case for higher: 0.16% in 2017 before the pandemic year (427,165 on the same base); 0.25% among Medicaid adults in 2020; the two-code rule misses patients not seen twice within a year (the paper's one-code rates are in a supplement not read). Case for lower: a 12-month washout counts some returning, already-diagnosed patients as new, and they already sit in the Walitt prevalence. Its effect on patients is contained: untreated_carryover_pct and penetration_peak_pct are re-derived on this basis
incidence.check: Researcher's 2,424,163 withdrawn and replaced. Weir 2006 abstract via PubMed confirms the rates (6.88 and 11.28 per 1,000 person-years, age-adjusted) and the arithmetic (9.08 per 1,000 x 266,978,268 = 2,424,163), but the cases are first claims coded ICD-9 729.1 in one insurer's 62,000 enrollees a year from 1997 to 2002, and 729.1 is the unspecified myalgia and myositis code. So the figure counts first coded myalgia, not new fibromyalgia diagnoses, and the source does not hold for the field. Kaur 2026 is fibromyalgia-specific (M79.7), US, adult, first-ever code with a 12-month lookback and two-code confirmation; 0.0012 x 266,978,268 = 320,373.9, so 320,374. The paper itself notes Weir-type estimates as the only earlier US figure.

eligible_pct.source: Liu Y et al., J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2016;22(3):263-271, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.3.263, PMID 27003556: of 240,144 US adults newly diagnosed with fibromyalgia (ICD-9 729.1, MarketScan 2009-2011), 'Only 31% (n = 74,738) initiated a treatment with a prescription medication listed in the ACR guidelines' within a year. 74,738 / 240,144 = 0.3112
eligible_pct.note: Judgement: one filter, the share of diagnosed patients who start a guideline prescription drug, the population a prescription label reaches (the seltorexant seed's 'treated' filter, the same idea). It is measured on the same ICD-9 729.1 definition as the incidence. FORWARD's entry criteria are adults 18 or over with a fibromyalgia diagnosis (Axsome Q2 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-341206); no line or biomarker applies, and I could not open its full severity thresholds (the Pfizer Phase 2 required pain of 40mm or more on a 100mm VAS and a weekly mean of 4 or more; Arnold LM et al., Clin Ther 2010, PMID 20974319). Case for lower: the trials enrol patients meeting ACR criteria, and only 26.5% of the clinically diagnosed do (Walitt 2016, above); the label is expected to read 'management of fibromyalgia' like Savella's, and prescribers act on the clinical diagnosis, so that filter is not applied. Case for higher: 31% is the first year after diagnosis, and more of the prevalent pool has been treated at some point. The filter cancels against penetration_peak_pct, which is solved on this same basis
eligible_pct.check: 74,738 / 240,144 = 0.31122; Liu 2016 abstract via PubMed: 'Only 31% (n = 74,738) initiated a treatment with a prescription medication listed in the ACR guidelines', within a year of first diagnosis. Against FORWARD: the only entry criteria I could read are 'at least 18 years of age with diagnosis of fibromyalgia' (Q2 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-341206; Amass was out of quota and the registry page is blocked). So 0.3112 is not a label or entry filter: under the label FORWARD implies, every diagnosed adult is reachable (1.0). It is a treatment-uptake filter, which the book accepts (seltorexant seed's 'Treated' 61%), and it cancels against penetration_peak_pct, which is solved on the same 0.3112 basis; dropping it would take the solved peak to about 1.3% for the same patients. Case for higher, beyond the researcher's: Liu measured the share on ICD-9 729.1, the broad myalgia code, so a M79.7-diagnosed pool probably starts guideline drugs more often. Judgement labelled with both cases; confirmed.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Savella, CMS Part D (lookup.py demand Savella): 16,373 beneficiaries in 2023 and 16,606 in 2024. New starts in 2024 = 16,606 - 16,373 x (1 - 0.75) = 12,513. Medicare pool on this seed's basis: 53.1mm Part D enrollees in 2024 (KFF, Key Facts About Medicare Part D Enrollment, Premiums, and Cost Sharing in 2024, the book's brenipatide value) x (1.78% diagnosed prevalence + 0.12% incidence, Kaur 2026) x 0.31122 (74,738 / 240,144) = 313,991, less the 16,373 already on Savella = 297,618. 12,513 / 297,618 = 4.204%
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Savella's 2024 capture. The same calculation gives 4.61% (2021), 4.26% (2022) and 4.07% (2023). Run through the engine's identity (k 0.574, midpoint 3, discontinuation 0.75), new starts peak near 54,000 a year around 2038 and the treated stock near 71,700 in 2039, about $256mm gross and $128mm net at the Savella price. Judgement also in applying the all-adult prevalence and incidence to Medicare enrollees; Kaur 2026 finds diagnosed prevalence rising with age to a peak at 70-79 in Commercial + Medicare, so the Medicare pool is if anything understated and this rate overstated. Case for lower, and it is quantified: Savella's US sales were about $102.9mm in the 12 months to January 2026 (IQVIA, cited in Breckenridge's generic launch release, March 2026), against $59.3mm of Medicare Part D spend alone in 2024, so Medicare is over half its sales; applying the Medicare capture rate to all adults sizes a Savella-equivalent at about $298mm gross (16,606 x 266,978,268 / 53.1mm x $3,572), 2.9x its measured national size. Generic milnacipran from March 2026 also cheapens the class incumbent. Case for higher: Savella in 2024 is 15 years past launch and barely promoted, and its Medicare users fell 13% from 19,099 in 2020; Axsome promotes to the same prescribers; Tonmya's prescriptions doubled quarter on quarter to 12,592 in Q2 2026 (Tonix Q2 2026 release); Axsome claims $0.5-1B peak sales for AXS-14 (Q2 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-341206). Case for lower also: AXS-14 arrives after Tonmya into a market led by generic duloxetine, pregabalin and gabapentin
penetration_peak_pct.check: Researcher's arithmetic reproduces on its own basis: 53.1mm x (0.0178 + 0.00908) x 0.311222 = 444,215; 444,215 - 16,373 = 427,842; 12,512.75 / 427,842 = 0.029246, and 3.20% / 2.96% / 2.83% for 2021-2023. Re-solved on the corrected incidence (0.12%), which the engine adds to the same pool: 313,991 - 16,373 = 297,618; 12,512.75 / 297,618 = 0.042043. Patients barely move (engine peak stock about 71,700 against about 82,300 on the old inputs), as the researcher said. Savella beneficiaries 19,099 / 18,374 / 17,195 / 16,373 / 16,606 (2020-2024) confirmed in the book. The researcher's statement that the output matches Savella's own national size by construction does not hold against IQVIA's $102.9mm (seen in search results for the Breckenridge release and a second report of a $103M market), so it is replaced in the note by that quantified case for lower; the method is the house one (CMS beneficiaries over the pool) and is kept.

untreated_carryover_pct.source: derived to hold the pool at its measured size, the method the remternetug and direclidine seeds use: retention = prevalence / (prevalence + inflow) = 4,752,213 / (4,752,213 + 320,374) = 0.9368
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. Fibromyalgia is chronic and the engine has no exit from the untreated pool, so at full carryover the M79.7 inflow would grow the diagnosed pool by 6.7% a year past its measured prevalence. Holding it stationary is the book's answer, and it implies 6.3% of the untreated pool leaves each year (remission, loss to care, death, or diagnosis lapsing). The case against: that exit is unmeasured, and on the 2017 incidence (0.16%) the same method gives 0.9175
untreated_carryover_pct.check: Recomputed the stated derivation: on the researcher's inputs 4,752,213 / (4,752,213 + 2,424,163) = 0.6622, arithmetic right; but its inflow was the ICD-9 729.1 myalgia incidence, corrected above. On the corrected incidence 4,752,213 / 5,072,587 = 0.93684, so 0.9368. The eligible share multiplies both terms and cancels, as in the remternetug seed (15.87 / (15.87 + 1.95) = 0.8906). Judgement label kept.

ramp_steepness.source: reused from the brenipatide and seltorexant seeds (lookup.py seed Brenipatide): Auvelity CMS Part D beneficiaries 9,268 in 2023 to 16,448 in 2024, a step of 1.775x, so k = ln(1.775) = 0.574
ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured curve: Auvelity is Axsome's own oral CNS launch into a generic-dominated market, the closest launch the book carries to how Axsome would sell AXS-14. Judgement carried from the seed: it reads one yearly step as early exponential growth. No fibromyalgia launch curve exists in the book: Savella's CMS series starts in 2020, 11 years after launch, and Tonmya has three quarters of data. Tonmya's early uptake (prescriptions doubling quarter on quarter) is faster, but from a very small base
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py seed Brenipatide and Seltorexant both hold ramp_steepness 0.574 from Auvelity; lookup.py demand Auvelity: 9,268 (2023) and 16,448 (2024) Part D beneficiaries, ln(16,448 / 9,268) = ln(1.7747) = 0.5736. Reused measured curve, correctly attributed, judgement carried from the seed.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: reused from the brenipatide seed: Axsome FY2025 results (8-K, February 2026), Auvelity net sales up 74% in its third full year, Q4 2025 prescriptions up 42% year on year and 8% quarter on quarter
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Reused measured curve. Half of peak around 2033 on a 2030 start. Judgement carried from the seed; it rests on one launch
ramp_midpoint_year.check: lookup.py seed Brenipatide and Seltorexant hold ramp_midpoint_year 3.0. Axsome FY2025 results 8-K (0001193125-26-062421, book filing text): AUVELITY full-year 2025 net sales $507.1mm, 74% year-over-year growth; about 225,000 Q4 prescriptions, up 42% on Q4 2024 and 8% on Q3 2025. Reused measured curve; confirmed.
